newsitem.title: INDIA: Police arrest 179 protestors at India Enron plant.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 179 protestors at India Enron plant.

text.p: Police on Thursday arrested nearly 200 people in India's wealthiest state for holding a protest meeting at the site of a $2.3 billion power plant being built by U.S. multinational Enron Corp.

"There were totally 450 demonstrators, who shouted and waved banners and placards against the project," a spokesman for the National Alliance of People's Movements, which organised the protest, told Reuters.
Fishermen and farmers living in villages near the 2,450 MW plant at Dabhol in western Maharashtra state, 160 km (100 miles) south of Bombay, have said they fear it will destroy their livelihoods.
They believe effluents from the plant, spread over 700 hectares on the Arabian sea coast, will pollute their fields and orchards and kill off the fish.
Most of the protestors arrested were women, the spokesman said. Among them was Medha Patkar, a prominent Indian environmentalist who led the meeting.

Police officials said they had arrested 179 people. "This includes 108 women," a local police official told Reuters. "They have been arrested under the Bombay Police Act, and were being taken to court when reports last came in."
Maharashtra state on Tuesday announced plans to float a six-billion-rupee privately-placed bond issue to finance its purchase of 30 percent of the equity in the project from Enron.
The plant is being built by the Dabhol Power Co, an Enron subsidiary, in which Enron holds 80 percent of the equity and Bechtel Group Inc and General Electric Capital Services ten percent each.
